claims.claim: Staged verification (lightweight filters then ORM ranking) shifts the accuracy-throughput Pareto frontier outward, giving 11.64x higher throughput at 8.26% accuracy loss versus full test-suite verification.
claims.scope_conditions: Qwen 2.5 Coder Instruct generators, four Python benchmarks, best-of-64
claims.quoted_support: We find that ORMs with staged verification shift the Pareto frontier outward, achieving 11.64x higher throughput at a cost of 8.26% accuracy relative to full test-suite verification.

claims.claim: Results are averaged over six seeds with 95% CIs; median CI width 1.48 percentage points.
claims.quoted_support: Results are averaged over six random seeds with 95% confidence intervals; median CI width is 1.48 percentage points.

claims.claim: Both generators and ORM backbones are from the Qwen family, which may favor the ORM through distribution matching.
claims.quoted_support: While this ensures compatibility, it may favor the ORM through distribution matching; we partially address this via distribution-shift evaluation on HumanEval and MBPP.

claims.claim: Test-based filtering catches bugs the ORM misses: filtered candidates sat 31 ranks too high on average.
claims.quoted_support: Test-based filtering catches bugs the ORM misses, particularly single-character errors that preserve surface form but fail at runtime. Filtered candidates sat 31 ranks too high on average; removing them shifts the frontier.

breadth.confidence_families: Outcome reward models (learned Bradley-Terry-style scorer), majority voting, syntax/lint/N-test filters as verification signals (Section 3-4, Table 1). No verbal or hidden-state confidence of the generator.
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Qwen 2.5 Coder Instruct generators (7B training candidates; sizes 1.5B-14B in analyses) and Qwen-family ORM backbones (training section).
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present as a pair (Instruct generators only); searched: base.
breadth.post_training_stages: ORM trained 2 epochs with margin objective on pairs (4.7K CodeContests and 7.3K GSM8K problems); no RLHF of generators.
breadth.elicitation_formats: Best-of-64 sampling at temperatures with ORM ranking and staged filtering (Section 3-4).
breadth.benchmarks: Four Python benchmarks per Abstract; those named in text: CodeContests (training pairs 4.7K plus evaluation, LiveCodeBench-style STDIN format noted at Section on datasets), GSM8K (training pairs 7.3K), HumanEval and MBPP via EvalPlus (distribution-shift evaluation). The fourth benchmark is not identified in the text I read.
breadth.label_source: Test-suite execution (full suite as strong verifier).
breadth.label_independence: Distribution-shift evaluation on HumanEval and MBPP separate from CodeContests/GSM8K training problems (training section); six seeds.
breadth.contamination_split: not present (searched: contamination, release date; only distribution-shift split described)
breadth.calibration_metrics: not present (searched: ECE, Brier, calibration error; evaluation is accuracy (best-of-64) and throughput PPS)
breadth.granularity: Per-candidate program scoring; per-test pruning (N Test filters with first N tests).
breadth.causal_intervention: Filter ablations (syntax, lint, N tests) and temperature ablations (Tables 6-10); no model-internal intervention.
